title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the stratification at infinity of moduli spaces (Mg,ν bar and its normal-crossings boundary). The previous pages built finite étale maps from strata D_{d*}, indexed by multi-indices, onto skeleta Θ^{(d)}_{d'*}. This page finishes that point: D^*_{d*} is the inverse image of D^*_{\tilde d'*}, equivalently of Θ^{(d)*}_{d'*}.

It then states a general 'situation clef'.
- Setup: Y is a smooth complex-analytic space with a normal-crossings divisor Θ. Θ^{(k)} is its codimension-k skeleton, the locus where at least k local branches meet. Θ^{(k)*} is the open part where exactly k branches meet.
- Data: D'' and D' are smooth analytic spaces with maps D'' → D' → Y that are local immersions (locally closed embeddings up to finite étale ambiguity).
- Coherent reading of codimensions (the manuscript and margin are somewhat garbled): D' has codimension d_0 in Y and factors through Θ^{(d_0)}. D'' has codimension d_1 in Y and factors through Θ^{(d_1)}. So D'' sits in D' with codimension d = d_1 − d_0, where d_1 > d_0 ≥ 0; the margin notes the case d_0 = 0 (D' open in Y) is allowed but trivial.
- D''* and D'* denote the inverse images of the open strata Θ^{(d_1)*} and Θ^{(d_0)*}. Along D''*, Θ is locally a union of d_1 smooth branches crossing transversally along D''.
- To each local immersion he attaches the 'multinormal principal bundle' P_D. This is the (C*)^k-torsor (or real-torus analogue) given by the product of the normal line bundles of the k local branches, minus their zero sections. Its fundamental group is an extension of π1(D*) by Z^k, the local inertia/Dehn-twist lattice.
- He considers the fundamental groupoids of these bundles. On the next page he announces a canonical 'generalization' morphism γ_{D'',D'}: π1 P_{D''*} → π1 P_{D'*}. This is the transport from the punctured normal data of a deeper stratum to that of a shallower stratum containing it, i.e. the inclusion of vertex groups at infinity into edge or less-degenerate groups.

In modern terms, P_{D*} is homotopy-equivalent to the boundary torus bundle of the Kato–Nakayama (real oriented blow-up) space over the open stratum. γ is the cospecialization map between fundamental groups of these torus bundles over adjacent strata. Tangential base points at a deep stratum are thereby transported to those at a shallower one. The aim is the 'structure at infinity' of the Teichmüller/mapping-class groupoids: how the Z^d-extended groups of boundary strata assemble into a compatible system (the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse).
errors: Codimension bookkeeping on the page is inconsistent. It says D''* has codimension d_0, D'' has codimension d_1, and D' factors through Θ^{(d_1)} while D''* factors through Θ^{(d_0)*}. Only the reading D' ⊂ Θ^{(d_0)}, D'' ⊂ Θ^{(d_1)}, codim(D'',D') = d_1 − d_0 is coherent, since the deeper stratum must have the larger codimension.
'Squelette de dimension d_1' should be 'codimension d_1', as the next line itself says.

ideas.what: Multinormal principal bundle attached to a local immersion of a stratum of a normal-crossings divisor: the product of punctured normal line bundles of the branches, a (C*)^k-torsor.
ideas.modern_name: Deleted normal bundle / torus bundle of the Kato–Nakayama log space over a stratum; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Kato–Nakayama (log Betti space, 1999); Ihara–Nakamura for Mg,n bar (1997)
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, 'points base à l'infini'), but not this formalism

ideas.what: Canonical 'generalization' morphism γ_{D'',D'} from π1 of the multinormal bundle of a deeper stratum to that of a shallower one.
ideas.modern_name: Cospecialization / generalization maps between local fundamental groups at boundary strata (log fundamental group, Kato–Nakayama, Illusie–Kato–Nakayama)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (SGA 7 cospecialization); log geometry school (1990s); Nakamura on boundary of Teichmüller modular groups

ideas.what: Strata of the boundary map finite-étale onto skeleta Θ^{(d)}; open parts are inverse images of open skeleta.
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of strata of a normal-crossings divisor

missed.claim: A general formalism, for any normal-crossings pair (Y,Θ) and any pair of nested strata, of fundamental groups of 'multinormal principal bundles' with canonical generalization morphisms. This is meant as the backbone of the structure at infinity of Mg,ν, anticipating the functoriality of log fundamental groups (Kato–Nakayama) and of tangential base points along all boundary strata.
missed.quote: On considère les "fibrés principaux multinormaux" P_{D''}, P_{D'}, associés aux immersions locales D'' → Y, D' → Y, et les groupoïdes fondamentaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Grothendieck's construction (promised on later pages) could be compared with the log-étale/Kato–Nakayama treatment and with Nakamura/Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps work on the Teichmüller groupoid. It may contain an organized system of compatibilities among all strata not written down explicitly in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent pre-log-geometry formalism (torus bundles over strata, generalization maps between their π1) aimed at the Teichmüller tower. It is conceptually close to later published notions (tangential base points, Kato–Nakayama), so it is not genuinely new. It is a notable unpublished detail of how Grothendieck set up 'structure à l'infini'.
transcription_corrections: The struck line likely reads 'Commençons par un diagramme'; the next line reads 'finalement, ... et revenir dans la'.
Codimension labels in the 'Situation clef' are garbled: the image suggests D'' of codimension d_1 factoring through Θ^{(d_1)}, D'* through Θ^{(d_0)*}, and D''* of codimension d = d_1 − d_0 in D'.
The margin reads 'd_1 > d_0 ≥ 0 (cas d_0 = 0 non exclus, mais ... trivial)'. Its diagram shows D''* → D'* with étale vertical maps to D_{d_0,d_1} → D_{d_1} and D'* → D_0 = pt.
'P_{D''}, P_{D'}' are probably meant with stars (P_{D''*}, P_{D'*}), as on the next page.
